reviews.text:
I went to the Menya Sandaime Hongdae main branch in Hongdae.
If you like Japanese ramen, this is a place that will satisfy you 🍜
The ramen broth was thick but not too greasy, so I was able to enjoy it until the end, and the noodles were chewy, so they went well with the broth.
The chashu was soft and well-boiled without any unpleasant smell, so each piece was impressive.
The gyoza we ordered together was crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, so it went well with the ramen.
The char siu rice bowl had a generous amount of meat and was seasoned just right, making it a perfect meal 🍚
The atmosphere of the store was clean and the staff were friendly, so it was great for a quick meal alone or with friends.
If you are looking for a proper Japanese ramen, gyoza, and char siu rice bowl restaurant in Hongdae, I recommend Menya Sandaime Hongdae Main Branch.
I am 100% willing to revisit 😋🔥

Eat about 25 or more bowls for dinner at unlimited refill conveyor belt sushi. At the self-service bar, you can sample unlimited salads, stir-fried ketchup rotini appetizers, desserts, various fried foods, tteokbokki, and miso soup. However, unlimited soda is available for an additional 2,000 won. You cannot have carbonated drinks without additional cost. Some alcoholic beverages are also available.
There are a variety of sushi available, and sometimes you can catch white fish sushi. The quality of the white fish was better than expected (I presume sea bream was also served). Not only are they served with hanchi, soy sauce shrimp, and various kinds of shrimp, but they also serve several versions of salmon sushi. The salmon that came with toro salmon (salmon belly) was the most delicious. Tuna was also caught occasionally, and although there was akami, it seems that jutoro was also caught. I ate 4 bowls of miso soup and sampled small amounts of appetizers and fried foods. Taste is okay.
Meanwhile, rolls were also served occasionally, and the roll taste was good. Now that I think about it, it feels like it’s been a while since I ate a roll. I think I often come here when I want to eat a lot of sushi.
Disappointing) The ginger is thin and small, so it is not suitable for use as a soy sauce spread on sushi. We have no choice but to choose the primitive method of eating sushi dipped in soy sauce. I keep thinking about brushes.
Hint) Like the reviews say, some of it tastes like sea salt. This has to be caught with wasabi. There are many different versions of salmon, but you can't go wrong with salmon with belly fat~ haha.

This is the place to go when you want to truly taste yakitori. As a yakitori enthusiast, I recognize this place! It's a place I want to save because I'm afraid I won't be able to go if it gets too popular. I was impressed from the first skewer, Tsukune. Tsukune is often used as a symbol of each yakitori restaurant. What makes it special is that it contains oyster bones, and the seasoning is not as dark as you might think. It's impressive that they give you an hourglass to tell you to eat before it gets cold. If you eat it all within that time, it may not pass as a drink snack, but it definitely passes in terms of taste and sensibility.
Make a reservation and get a guaranteed seat!! I have to come again. If there's anyone who enjoys drinking sake by the bottle, that person is probably me.

reviews.text:
#Hongdae #Sangsu-dong #Masterpiece

“Something wild Jjajangmyeon and dumplings”

It is a fairly well-known Chinese restaurant in the Hongdae area.
It's not a shabby Chinese restaurant, but it's popular because it's quite tasty and easy to drink, and they sometimes hold discount events, so it's popular with students.

This restaurant's Jjajangmyeon is a bit unique, and the newly released meat Jjajang can be considered the restaurant's style of soybean jjajang.
Immediately place a generous amount of sliced ​​meat on top of the stir-fried jjajang.
I was drawn to this uniqueness and visited this house.

#mood
It has a pub atmosphere.
It seems that they are still using the place that used to be a bar (pocha atmosphere impersonating an izakaya).
The cherry blossom decorations on the wall are still there.
So it doesn't feel like an open interior, but rather a feeling of being divided into rooms.
It's a bit difficult for the servers, but it's not bad for shy customers or those who drink because they have a sense of independence.

#Meat Jjajang
This is not the style of putting meat on top of the jjajang you made.
It would be a terrible restaurant to serve water jjajang at the high price of 10,000 won, but it is different from regular jajangmyeon because it is stir-fried right away like soy sauce.
The intestines are thick and the taste is quite rich.
Among the sweet, salty, and savory flavors, the sweet taste is dominant, but the overall flavor is strong and strong, so the prominence of the sweet taste is not annoying.
There was a lot of boiled pork on top to emphasize the chewy taste of the meat.
A strategy that kills two birds with one stone by complementing the texture and enhancing the visual appearance.

The texture is a bit disappointing.
Maybe it's because of the long frying time, but the onions are soft, so it doesn't quite reach the level of a well-made soybean paste, but the meat filling makes up for it, so it's not bad.

#Grilled dumplings
One of the signature dishes of this restaurant is fried dumplings.
You can order only one plate of handmade dumplings per table.
You can order half a plate, so it's also good for solo eaters.
It is quite large in size, but the dumpling skin is thin, so the breadiness of the dumpling is expressed well.
You can feel the richness of the dumpling filling without it being too heavy, but the lightness of the filling mainly made of chives and meat is the main flavor.
Light dumplings that do not rely on seasoning go harmoniously with the intensity of Jjajangmyeon.
Pretty delicious fried dumplings.

I like the uniqueness of this house.
It is by no means an ordinary, half-baked house, but a house where the master's cooking philosophy and style are expressed through techniques.
I need to go further and try some other dishes.

reviews.author: Chanwook Lee
reviews.text:
Panelo, Spacca Napoli, Hongdae, Sangsu, and Hapjeongkwon are truly battlegrounds for Neapolitan-style oven pizza. There are many places I haven't been to yet, but I visited Brett Pizza, which I was most curious about.

I made a reservation on a weekday evening through Catch Table without a separate deposit, and there were plenty of seats, but since the store is not large, it would be better to make a reservation on the weekend. It is located in the semi-basement of the house.

It has a modern Italian restaurant atmosphere rather than a casual atmosphere like Pitjeria, and in addition to pizza, they also serve a few types of pasta. The price is a bit high, but we only ate one pizza per person.

Since beer is a must with pizza, I had a large glass of Stella Artois with it, and it was a bit disappointing that it didn't come in a special glass. The alcoholic beverage lineup is quite diverse, including beer, wine, and spirits.

When it comes to Neapolitan pizza restaurants, there is absolutely no Margherita. Because the toppings are simple, just tomatoes, basil, and cheese, they are used as a measure of pizza taste and skill.

In the case of Margherita, I was very familiar with it, but it was a lot of fun because they provided an explanation card for each pizza I ordered. The harmony of the aforementioned tomatoes, basil, and cheese is the key to Margherita.

As expected from a well-made margherita, the taste was light and savory, and the olive oil added to the flavor. The dough was moist, but the gorniczone was crispy and unique, like grilled focaccia.

After demonstrating my skills with the Margherita, I next tried the Harclet, the original pizza of this place. Hacklet is a pizza made with potato puree as a base and topped with cheese, cabbage, and prosciutto.

The explanation card says it's high in calories, but that's inevitable because there are so many ingredients included. It seems like there will be a lot of people who like it and dislike it because of the bitter gourd crop, but personally, it was delicious.

Thanks to the pureed potatoes, it wasn't too heavy, and the cabbage added vitality to the puree. It seemed light, but had the salty and savory taste unique to raclette cheese.

One pizza per person wasn't enough, so we ended the meal happily with a small glass of Stella Artois. Margherita was faithful to the basics, and Harclet was an unexpected discovery.

reviews.text:
ASAP Pizza Hongdae: A perfect meal with New York street vibes and slices!
'ASAP Pizza', located in the middle of Hongdae's hipster street, is, as its name suggests, "As Soon As Possible," meaning it is a place you go to without hesitation when you want to eat pizza quickly. The hip and trendy atmosphere is impressive, as if it were a replica of a casual pizza place in Brooklyn, New York.
The charm of slice pizza, various flavors at once
The biggest attraction of ASAP Pizza is that it sells pizza by the slice. Whether you eat alone or with a group of people, you can easily try a variety of flavors, giving you a wide range of choices. The generous toppings on top of the thick yet chewy dough are satisfying to the eye.
The most recommended menu item is the classic of classics, pepperoni pizza. The combination of salty and juicy pepperoni and rich cheese is a taste that calls for beer or cold cola. If you want something a little more special, try the richly flavored truffle pizza or sweet and salty Hawaiian pizza.
Great atmosphere, perfect for a date
The pizza is quickly heated upon ordering and is served piping hot and perfect. The interior is full of cool and stylish design, making it a perfect photo spot to take pictures while eating delicious pizza.
Since it's open until late, it's perfect for a late-night snack when you're hungry after hanging out in Hongdae. If you want to experience the free sensibility of New York and delicious pizza at the same time, visit ASAP Pizza Hongdae!
